title: LoFT-LLM: Low-Frequency Time-series Forecasting with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Real-world time-series forecasting must handle limited training data, complex noisy temporal dynamics, and high-frequency noise that obscures long-term trends.

gap.claim: Existing approaches underutilize auxiliary variables with domain-specific information, particularly in few-shot settings.

contributions.claim: LoFT-LLM is a frequency-aware forecasting pipeline that combines low-frequency learning with LLM-based semantic calibration.
A Patch Low-Frequency forecasting Module extracts stable low-frequency trends from localized spectral patches, followed by residual learning for high-frequency variations.
A fine-tuned LLM refines predictions using auxiliary context and domain knowledge expressed through structured natural-language prompts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on financial and energy datasets reportedly show that LoFT-LLM significantly outperforms strong baselines in full-data and few-shot settings.
The authors report superior accuracy, robustness, and interpretability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world forecasting is difficult because data may be limited and temporal dynamics may be complex and noisy.
Full-window supervision can preserve high-frequency noise and obscure long-term trends, while auxiliary variables are often underused.
LoFT-LLM combines low-frequency trend extraction, residual modeling of high-frequency variation, and LLM-based semantic calibration.
The authors report improvements over strong baselines across financial and energy datasets and both full-data and few-shot regimes.

source_observation.claim: The method separates stable low-frequency trends from high-frequency residual variation before applying semantic calibration.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting pipelines may benefit from assigning distinct modeling stages to different frequency components and contextual information.

application.claim: For noisy, data-limited forecasting tasks, consider combining frequency decomposition with structured use of auxiliary domain context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers beyond the reported financial and energy settings.

unknowns: Dataset names, sizes, and preprocessing details are not provided.
Forecast horizons, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and numerical results are not provided.
The LLM architecture, fine-tuning procedure, and prompt structure are not described.
Statistical significance, ablations, and computational costs are not reported.
